Unsupported postposed 按周/季度/年计 cannot expose 4000 as a total or supported enum rate, including source layout and stored exact values.
Date-only cue/bridge spelling view supports the same employment, wage-period and contract-signing roles without rewriting dates.
Explicit +奖金/加上加班费/乘以提成 leave base operands unavailable across value, quote, source and stored-state paths.
Qualifiers on a duration or unrelated noun no longer suppress the single exact wage token; an actual attached monetary bound still stays unavailable.

notes: The previous whole-string APPROXIMATE branch is removed in favor of the already shared token-edge qualifier grammar; inner 多/余 retains conservative handling when no exact token matches. A frozen legacy approximate result cannot overwrite a newly exact token.

Financial glyph aliases occur only after the original token is located. Numeral boundary checks, range detection copy, and arithmetic detection copy recognize the same finite new glyphs; source quotes, candidate representation, raw response and Unicode code-point positions are preserved.

Unsupported postposed rates are a separate null-unit result. Each supported or unsupported candidate checks its own complete right boundary; a supported prefix cannot consume 月 within an unknown unit. Source review inspects existing layout edges and does not trust model subjects to waive the guard.
Date-only aliasing is downstream of original literal owner and period/value positions. Signing is not converted to employment, and the collective-subject guard is unchanged.

Named payroll operands require the existing explicit operator path, a bounded Han component ending and a complete word boundary. Sentence separators and other people remain outside the attachment grammar. No formula is evaluated.

Source review still only reduces stored availability. These tests exercise explicitly forced old exact values as downgrade inputs and old unsupported values as no-upgrade controls. Accepted review candidates and amount fields never create confirmations or calculation authority.
